name: WHAM!
ability_definition: The ability to focus on a single source of sound in the presence of other distracting sounds.

task_realism.reasoning: Isolating speech from competing talkers and real urban noise (cafés, restaurants, bars, parks) matches the core challenge of auditory attention in noisy workplaces. However, the mixtures are synthetic: read Wall Street Journal sentences are digitally summed at controlled levels. There is no reverberation (that is WHAMR!), no conversational turn-taking, no far-field microphones, and at most two speakers. Real settings like dispatch floors, call centers, or crowded job sites are messier and more varied.

evaluation_conditions.reasoning: Evaluation is offline on pre-segmented, heavily overlapped utterances. The number of speakers is fixed and known, the audio is 8 kHz, and the model sees the whole clip with no latency constraint. Real work involves streaming audio, an unknown and changing number of sources, and a continuous need to attend over long periods. SNRs of -6 to +3 dB are realistically hard, but the input distribution is narrow and matches the training data.

construct_coverage.reasoning: It measures one important slice: separating overlapping voices from noise. It does not measure selective, cue-driven focus on a single chosen target, which is closer to target speaker extraction. It also omits sustained tracking of one source over time, switching attention, and attending to non-speech targets such as alarms or machine sounds. SI-SNRi captures signal fidelity, not whether the attended content was actually usable.

format_match.reasoning: Audio goes in and separated audio comes out, which is a natural format with no forced choice or toy grid. However, the output is an intermediate waveform scored by a signal metric. In real work, the product of attending is comprehension or action on the target stream, which this benchmark never tests.

transferability_reasoning: WHAM! directly tests pulling speech out of competing voices and real noise, so it is well aligned with the perceptual core of auditory attention. Transfer is limited by synthetic two-speaker mixtures of read speech, offline evaluation with a known speaker count, separation of all speakers rather than cued focus on one, and a signal-fidelity metric instead of task-relevant use of the attended stream.

2021.metric: dB SI-SNRi (scale-invariant signal-to-noise ratio improvement), WHAM! test set, 8 kHz min mode
2021.human_reference: General adult listeners with normal hearing. Auditory attention is a general ability used in everyday work settings such as offices, phone calls, meetings and noisy workplaces.
